title: AVoCaDO: An Audiovisual Video Captioner Driven by Temporal Orchestration
claim: Naively combining separately generated per-modality descriptions loses cross-modal information that a single time-aligned joint description preserves, changing downstream answers.
layout: Top video strip, two caption panels, question and model bottom-left, bar chart bottom-right
description: A pilot-experiment schematic. At the top, a film strip of video frames shows a woman singing in military uniform. Speech and audio transcripts sit beneath the strip. Two colored dashed boxes branch from it. The blue box on the left, 'Separate AV caption', splits into a video caption and an audio caption. The green box on the right, 'Joint AV caption', is one interleaved time-aligned narrative. Both boxes contain underlined key phrases. Arrows lead from both boxes to a multiple-choice question in the bottom left, then to a Gemini answerer. The separate path gives 'Answer: N/A' with a blue cross, and the joint path gives 'Answer: B' with a green check. A bar chart at bottom right, 'Performance Comparison on the Daily-Omni Benchmark', compares the two caption types across categories. Red arrows mark the gaps, Δ=27.8 and Δ=15.8.
caption: Schematic illustration of the pilot experiment. In this example, naively concatenating captions from the video and audio modalities fails to yield a correct answer to the corresponding question. In contrast, jointly processing both modalities to generate a time-aligned caption provides sufficient information, as indicated by the underlined text.
abstract: Audiovisual video captioning aims to generate semantically rich descriptions with temporal alignment between visual and auditory events, thereby benefiting both video understanding and generation. In this paper, we present AVoCaDO, a powerful audiovisual video captioner driven by the temporal orchestration between audio and visual modalities. We propose a two-stage post-training pipeline: (1) AVoCaDO SFT, which fine-tunes the model on a newly curated dataset of 107K high-quality, temporally-aligned audiovisual captions; and (2) AVoCaDO GRPO, which leverages tailored reward functions to further enhance temporal coherence and dialogue accuracy while regularizing caption length and reducing collapse. Experimental results demonstrate that AVoCaDO significantly outperforms existing open-source models across four audiovisual video captioning benchmarks, and also achieves competitive performance on the VDC and DREAM-1K benchmark under visual-only settings.
